description: A personal Kanban board with terminal/hacker aesthetic — monospace fonts, green-on-black, CLI-inspired UI. Three columns (To Do / In Progress / Done) with drag-and-drop, localStorage persistence, and keyboard shortcuts.

userStories.title: Project setup and terminal aesthetic board layout
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my task board styled like a terminal so that it feels fast and immersive.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a Next.js 14+ app with TypeScript strict mode in /workspace/app directory
Configure TailwindCSS with custom terminal color tokens: bg-terminal=#0a0a0a, bg-card=#0f1a0f, bg-column=#111811, text-primary=#00ff41, text-dim=#005c1a, text-accent=#39ff14, border=#00ff4133
Load JetBrains Mono via next/font/google and apply globally
Page renders three columns: [ TO_DO ], [ IN_PROGRESS ], [ DONE ] with terminal-styled headers
Background is #0a0a0a (black), all text uses JetBrains Mono monospace font
Primary text and accents are terminal green (#00ff41 or similar)
App title displayed as styled header: [ TASK_OS v1.0 ] in top bar
A blinking cursor (_) animation is present on the page
Keyboard shortcut legend visible: [N] NEW  [ESC] CANCEL  [DEL] DELETE
Full viewport height board with three equal-width scrollable columns
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Task data model and localStorage persistence
userStories.description: As a user, I want my tasks to persist across page reloads so I never lose my work.
acceptanceCriteria: Define Task TypeScript type with fields: id (uuid), title (string, required), description (string, optional), priority ('LOW' | 'MED' | 'HIGH', default 'MED'), status ('TODO' | 'IN_PROGRESS' | 'DONE'), createdAt (ISO timestamp)
Create useTaskStore custom hook that reads tasks from localStorage key 'task_os_tasks' on mount
All CRUD operations (create, update, delete, move) immediately write updated tasks to localStorage
If localStorage is empty, each column shows empty state: '> NO TASKS FOUND_'
Tasks are correctly distributed to columns based on status field
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Task card display with priority badges
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see task cards with priority badges so I can assess work at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: TaskCard component displays: title, priority badge, truncated description (if any), and action buttons [<<] [>>] [EDIT] [DEL]
Priority badge shown on card: [HIGH], [MED], [LOW]
Badge color coding: HIGH=#ff4444 (red), MED=#ffcc00 (yellow), LOW=#00aa33 (dim green)
All styled consistently with terminal aesthetic: monospace font, bracketed labels, green borders
Cards use bg-card=#0f1a0f background with terminal green border
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Create a new task
userStories.description: As a user, I want to add a new task to any column so that I can track new work.
acceptanceCriteria: Each column has an [+ ADD TASK] button at the bottom
Clicking it opens an inline form styled as a terminal prompt: '> ENTER TASK:_'
Task requires a non-empty title (show error if empty on submit)
Optional fields: description (textarea), priority select (LOW | MED | HIGH, default MED)
On submit, task appears in the column immediately with a generated uuid and createdAt timestamp
Task is saved to localStorage
Press Escape to cancel and close the form
Form inputs styled as terminal prompts with green text on dark background
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Edit an existing task
userStories.description: As a user, I want to edit a task's title, description, and priority so that I can keep it up to date.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking [EDIT] on a task card opens an edit modal styled as a terminal editor
All fields (title, description, priority) are editable in the modal
Save button (or Enter) persists changes to localStorage and closes modal
Cancel button (or Escape) discards changes and closes modal
Modal styled with terminal aesthetic: dark background, green borders, monospace font
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Delete a task with confirmation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to delete a task I no longer need.
acceptanceCriteria: Each task card has a [DEL] button
Clicking [DEL] shows an inline terminal-style confirmation: '> CONFIRM DELETE? [Y/N]_'
Pressing Y or clicking [Y] removes the task from the board and localStorage
Pressing N, Escape, or clicking [N] leaves the task untouched
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Move tasks via quick-action arrow buttons
userStories.description: As a user, I want arrow buttons on each card to move tasks left/right without dragging.
acceptanceCriteria: Cards in IN_PROGRESS and DONE show a [<<] button to move left to the previous column
Cards in TO_DO and IN_PROGRESS show a [>>] button to move right to the next column
Clicking [<<] or [>>] moves the task to the adjacent column instantly
New status is persisted to localStorage immediately
TO_DO cards have no [<<] button; DONE cards have no [>>] button
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Drag-and-drop tasks between columns
userStories.description: As a user, I want to drag tasks between columns to update their status.
acceptanceCriteria: Install @dnd-kit/core and configure DndContext wrapping the board
Task cards are draggable using @dnd-kit/core useDraggable hook
Each column is a drop target using @dnd-kit/core useDroppable hook
Drop target column is visually highlighted (brighter border or background) during drag
Task status updates immediately on drop and persists to localStorage
Works on desktop with mouse drag
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Keyboard shortcut N to create a task
userStories.description: As a user, I want to press N to quickly start adding a task without reaching for the mouse.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing N (when not focused in an input/textarea field) opens the new task form in the TO_DO column
The shortcut does not trigger when user is typing in any input or textarea
Keyboard shortcut legend visible on page: [N] NEW  [ESC] CANCEL  [DEL] DELETE
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
